key_insight: In β-Sn, absorbed ⟨c⟩ dislocations can drive twin-boundary faceting along (301) TBs, with facet length increasing as more dislocations are absorbed.
engineering_relevance: This mechanism helps explain deformation and strengthening in Sn-based solder alloys, where twin boundaries and dislocations strongly influence reliability.
method: Molecular dynamics simulations using a machine-learned interatomic potential (MLIP).
Dislocation-absorption modeling at (301) twin boundaries in β-Sn.
Elasticity-based interpretation that includes the disclination character of the asymmetric twin facet.
evidence_signal: The MD results reproduce a dislocation-driven faceting trend and match isotropic elasticity predictions only when disclination effects are included.
watch_item: The facet-length prediction depends on an elasticity idealization, so transferability beyond the simulated β-Sn twin geometry and loading conditions may be limited.
paper_title: Dislocation mediated twin boundary faceting in $β$-Sn
